title: Dwarkadhish Temple, Dwarka - A Divine Journey to the Abode of Lord Krishna
content:
Dwarkadhish Temple, Dwarka

Dwarkadhish Temple, also known as Jagat Mandir, is one of the most sacred Hindu temples in India. Located in Dwarka, Gujarat, this temple is dedicated to Lord Krishna, who is worshipped here as King of Dwarka or “Dwarkadhish”.

This ancient temple is not only a spiritual destination but also a marvel of architecture, mythology, and Indian heritage. If you're planning a religious trip or exploring famous temples in India, Dwarkadhish Temple must be on your list!

Where is Dwarkadhish Temple Located?

Dwarkadhish Temple is situated in the holy city of Dwarka, in the Devbhoomi Dwarka district of Gujarat, India. It is located on the Gomti River banks and is one of the four sacred Char Dham pilgrimage sites.

History and Significance

The temple has a rich mythological and historical background:

It is believed to be over 2,000 years old, with the current structure rebuilt in the 16th century.

According to legend, Lord Krishna established the city of Dwarka after leaving Mathura and ruled here as a king.

The temple is a key part of the Char Dham Yatra and Sapta Puri - the seven most ancient and sacred pilgrimage centers in India.

Temple Architecture

The architecture of Dwarkadhish Temple is a blend of Chalukya style and Maru-Gurjara style, with impressive carvings and grandeur:

Height: Approximately 78 meters

Main Spire (Shikhara): Visible from miles away

Flag: A 52-yard long multi-colored flag with symbols of the sun and moon is changed five times a day

Five-Storied Structure: Supported by 72 pillars

What to Expect Inside the Temple

Inside the temple, the main deity is Lord Krishna, adorned with royal attire and ornaments. The idol is in black marble and holds a conch (shankh), mace (gada), lotus (padma), and wheel (chakra).

Other nearby shrines in the temple complex are dedicated to: Rukmini Devi (Krishna’s consort), Balarama (Krishna’s brother), Radha, Vishnu, Devaki and Vasudeva

How to Reach Dwarkadhish Temple

  • By Air: The nearest airport is Jamnagar Airport (about 130 km away).
  • By Train: Dwarka has its own railway station, well-connected to major cities like Ahmedabad, Mumbai, and Delhi.
  • By Road: Regular buses and taxis are available from major cities in Gujarat.

Temple Timings

  • Morning: 6:30 AM to 1:00 PM
  • Evening: 5:00 PM to 9:30 PM
  • Aarti Timings: Early morning (Mangla Aarti) and evening aartis are popular with devotees.

Best Time to Visit

The best time to visit Dwarkadhish Temple is between October and March when the weather is pleasant. The temple is beautifully decorated during Janmashtami, the birth celebration of Lord Krishna.

Travel Tips

  • Dress modestly to respect the religious customs.
  • Photography is restricted inside the temple.
  • Visit early in the morning or late evening to avoid crowds.
  • Don’t miss the Gomti Ghat and Rukmini Devi Temple, nearby attractions.
